rows.question: Can you cancel my car insurance after I've had it for six months?
rows.answer:
**Yes, but only for specific reasons.** Once your policy has been in effect for more than 60 days, as yours has at six months, we will cancel only for nonpayment of premium, or if your driver's license or that of any driver who lives with you or customarily uses your covered auto has been suspended or revoked, or if the policy was obtained through material misrepresentation.

**The three permitted reasons, in plain terms:**
- **You haven't paid your premium.** You would get at least 10 days' notice before cancellation.
- **A license was suspended or revoked.** This applies to your license or the license of any driver who lives with you or regularly uses your car. You would get at least 20 days' notice before cancellation.
- **The policy was obtained through material misrepresentation**, meaning important information on the application was false. You would get at least 20 days' notice before cancellation.

These notice periods come from the policy: Notice for nonpayment is at least 10 days; for any other reason, at least 20 days.

**How you'd be notified:** We may cancel this policy by mailing notice to the named insured.

For comparison, the rules are looser early on. If the policy has been in effect less than 60 days, we will give at least 10 days notice. That broader early-cancellation window no longer applies to you.

This describes what the policy language says. Whether a particular cancellation is valid would depend on the specific facts.

rows.question: My tires got damaged by a pothole. Will collision pay?
rows.answer:
**If the damage is limited to your tires, the policy language excludes it, so collision coverage would not pay.** The policy says it will not pay for damage due and confined to wear and tear, freezing, mechanical or electrical breakdown or failure, or road damage to tires. A tire damaged by a pothole is road damage to tires.

**If the pothole also damaged other parts of your car** (for example, a wheel or the suspension), that exclusion wouldn't apply to those parts, because it covers only damage "confined to" the tires. Whether collision coverage applies to that other damage depends on a few things:

- **Whether you have Collision Coverage.** The policy pays for collision losses only if the Declarations indicate that Collision Coverage is provided. Check your Declarations page.
- **Whether the event counts as a "collision."** The policy defines collision as the upset of your covered auto or a non-owned auto or their impact with another vehicle or object. The policy doesn't say whether hitting a pothole counts as an impact with an "object," so I can't tell you that it would.
- **Your deductible.** Any payment is minus any applicable deductible shown in the Declarations.
- **How payment is figured.** The most the policy pays is the lesser of the actual cash value of the stolen or damaged property, or the amount necessary to repair or replace the property with other property of like kind and quality.

This explains the policy wording, not a final coverage decision. If there's damage beyond the tires, report the claim so an adjuster can review the details.

rows.question: How long after a hailstorm can I still file a claim?
rows.answer:
**In Texas, you generally have one year from the date of the hailstorm to report the claim.** The Texas Windstorm and Hail Deductible Endorsement says a claim for windstorm or hail damage must be reported to us within one year after the date of the windstorm or hail event, unless good cause exists for later reporting. If you're past the one-year mark, a later report is allowed only if there is good cause for the delay.

**Report as soon as you can.** Your homeowners policy also lists duties after a loss, including that you give prompt notice to us or our agent. After you report, protect the property from further damage and make reasonable and necessary repairs to protect it.

**Related time limits:**
- **Inspection:** We will inspect the damage within 15 days after receiving notice of the claim, unless a catastrophe has been declared, in which case the inspection period may be extended by 15 days.
- **Proof of loss:** If we ask for it, you must send to us, within 60 days after our request, your signed, sworn proof of loss.
- **Replacement cost:** You may make a claim on an actual cash value basis and then make a claim for any additional replacement cost within 180 days after the loss. For hail damage to your roof, this depends on the roof's age. Loss to roof surfacing caused by windstorm or hail is settled at actual cash value, not replacement cost, if the roof surfacing is more than 15 years old at the time of loss.

This explains what the policy language says. It is not a decision on whether a specific claim will be paid.

rows.question: The insured wants to invoke appraisal. What's my deadline to respond?
rows.answer:
You have two deadlines: **acknowledge the request in writing within 5 business days**, and **name the company appraiser within 20 days after receiving the insured's written request**.

**Internal guideline (CHG §4.3):** If the insured invokes appraisal, acknowledge the request in writing within 5 business days and name the company appraiser within the 20-day window in HO-3 Section 6.5.

**Policy language (HO-3 §6.5):**
- The 20-day clock starts when the written demand is received. Each party will choose a competent and impartial appraiser within 20 days after receiving a written request from the other. If the insured's demand was only verbal, confirm whether a written request has been received.
- Appraisal is available only for disputes over the amount of loss. If you and we fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal of the loss. It does not resolve coverage disputes.
- After both appraisers are named, the two appraisers will choose an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two will set the amount of loss.
- On costs, each party pays its own appraiser and shares equally the expense of the umpire.

No state endorsement applies here, so the base HO-3 timeframe governs.
